data.title: VIGGO Launches Mix1Pro Commercial Cleaning Robot at ISSA Show North America 2026
data.description:
VIGGO Launches Mix1Pro Commercial Cleaning Robot at ISSA Show North America 2026

VIGGO Launches Mix1Pro Commercial Cleaning Robot at ISSA Show North America 2026

PR Newswire

LAS VEGAS, Nov. 20, 2026

Full product lineup addresses cleaning needs across indoor facilities, parking garages and outdoor spaces.

LAS VEGAS, Nov. 20, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- VIGGO, a leading provider of commercial cleaning robots, showcased its full product lineup at ISSA Show North America 2026 (November 17–19), introducing its new Mix1Pro commercial cleaning robot to the global market.

The launch comes as commercial cleaning robots expand into more public spaces. According to IDC, global shipments reached approximately 58,000 units in 2025, an increase of 83.8% year over year. Building services, retail, transportation, hospitality and food service together accounted for 72.9% of shipments. For facility operators, long-term adoption depends on both cleaning performance and a robot's ability to adapt to changing conditions and work effectively alongside staff. Mix1Pro addresses these requirements through advances in navigation, cleaning and automated servicing.

Adaptive Navigation for Complex Environments

Mix1Pro combines 3D LiDAR with multi-sensor fusion to deliver 360-degree spatial perception. By detecting surrounding structures and tracking changes in its environment, the robot supports stable localization and responsive obstacle avoidance in complex, dynamic spaces.

Versatile Floor Care in One Machine

Mix1Pro sweeps, scrubs, vacuums and mops simultaneously in a single pass. Capable of both hard-floor care and carpet vacuuming, it accommodates diverse surfaces within a single facility. A 20.5-inch cleaning width supports efficient coverage, while an optional UV-C module adds disinfection capability.

Automated Servicing and Simpler Maintenance

Mix1Pro's fully automated docking station handles charging, clean-water refilling, wastewater draining, detergent dosing and self-cleaning of the scrubbing roller and roller brush. These functions reduce routine manual intervention and support extended autonomous operation.

A quick-release design simplifies daily maintenance, while an integrated ergonomic power-assisted handle and a 10-inch touchscreen make manual relocation and on-device operation more convenient.

Designed for shopping centers, supermarkets, hospitals, schools, hotels and office buildings, Mix1Pro accommodates varied floor types and cleaning requirements. Its quiet, efficient operation helps facilities maintain cleanliness alongside daily business activities and public services.

A Broader Portfolio for Specialized Cleaning Needs

Also on display were VIGGO's established product lines for other commercial environments.

The newly upgraded SC50ProPlus features hardware and software enhancements tailored to parking garages. Building on the SC50 series' versatility across indoor environments, these upgrades further strengthen its ability to sustain cleaning operations in these demanding settings.

The SC80 series draws on extensive deployment experience in industrial and logistics facilities across multiple international markets. Its long runtime and deep-cleaning capabilities address the demands of large areas and intensive cleaning schedules.

Designed for outdoor areas within enclosed or controlled-access sites, the S100-N is already operating across the Middle East, Europe and Asia. It provides autonomous sweeping for plazas, parks and roads within managed properties.

Practical Value for Facility Operators

VIGGO's commercial cleaning robot portfolio spans indoor and outdoor applications, with deployments in approximately 40 countries and regions. Sustained use across industrial facilities, transportation hubs and commercial properties has provided experience with a wide range of operating conditions.

From routine floor care to demanding cleaning tasks, the portfolio helps operators reduce manual workloads, simplify upkeep and maintain more consistent cleaning performance. By assigning repetitive cleaning work to robots, facilities can direct staff toward higher-value services and tasks requiring human judgment—improving both the quality of their spaces and the efficiency of their operations.

data.title: gategroup Successfully Completes EUR 120 Million Term Loan B Upsizing
data.description:
Zurich, Switzerland – November 20, 2026 – gategroup Holding AG (“gategroup”) is pleased to announce the successful completion of a EUR 120 million fully fungible add-on to its existing euro-denominated Term Loan B facility.

The transaction was well supported by a broad group of existing and new institutional investors, reflecting confidence in gategroup's resilient business model and its consistent operational and financial performance.

Urs Schwendinger, Group CFO, commented: "We are pleased with the strong investor support for this transaction. The additional funding strengthens our liquidity position, preserves flexibility for future growth opportunities and provides further optionality in addressing the upcoming CHF bond maturity.”

For media and investor inquiries, please contact:

IR@gategroup.com

mediacontact@gategroup.com

About gategroup
gategroup is a leading global provider of airline catering, retail-on-board, and hospitality products and services. Headquartered in Zurich, Switzerland, the company serves millions of passengers through a network of nearly 300 locations in more than 68 countries. By leveraging innovation and operational expertise, gategroup partners with the world’s leading airlines to create exceptional travel experiences. Learn more at www.gategroup.com

data.title: Nasdaq Set for Fresh Decline as AI Selloff Intensifies
data.description:
By Joe Stonor

Global stocks sold off and Treasurys strengthened as investor confidence in the artificial-intelligence trade showed signs of cracking.

Nasdaq futures dropped 1.15%, extending sharp falls from the last session. S&P 500 futures fell 0.5%, while contracts tied to the Dow Jones Industrial Average slipped 0.1%. Major U.S. indexes are on track for their worst week since the announcement of President Trump's Liberation Day tariffs upended global trade in April 2025.

Anthropic's record-breaking IPO failed to stem heavy selling across global stocks. Chip makers, tech giants and cloud-computing stocks weakened in U.S. premarket trade after heavy selling across Asian tech names. The memory chip-dominated Kospi closed 5.2% lower, while Japan's Nikkei also fell more than 5%. Taiwan's Taiex sank 6.2%, bringing its weekly loss to more than 17%--its worst week since 1990.

The selling bled to European stocks, too. ASML, the continent's most valuable stock, fell more than 5% as a basket of the continent's tech stocks opened 3% lower. The continent-wide Stoxx 600 was 1.2% lower.

Demand for Anthropic's IPO is focusing attention on the sustainability of the AI investment buildout while also draining liquidity from the broader market, said Roger Lee, head of equity strategy at Cavendish.

The gloominess in stock market sentiment comes despite fresh declines for oil. Benchmark Brent crude contracts dropped around 1.25% to $90.85 a barrel. West Texas Intermediate contracts fell 1.7% to trade around $81.80 a barrel. The U.S. Energy Information Administration said Thursday that oil shipments through major Middle Eastern shipping routes increased 19% in the third quarter.

Lower oil prices and an investor flight to safety combined to strengthen Treasurys. Ten-year yields fell back below 5.000%, while two-year yields dropped 6 basis points to 4.720%. Thirty-year yields fell 3.1 basis points to trade around 5.370%.

Metals prices continued to sell off, with gold tumbling close to 3% at $3,580 a troy ounce. The dollar held near multimonth highs, while bitcoin rebounded slightly but remained near July lows, hovering just below $62,000.

For the day ahead, macro watchers will look to Michigan's consumer sentiment index for November, and to Federal Reserve speakers including Christopher Waller.

Write to Joe Stonor at josephmichael.stonor@wsj.com

(END) Dow Jones Newswires

data.title: RLX Technology Announces Unaudited Third Quarter 2026 Financial Results
data.description:
RLX Technology Announces Unaudited Third Quarter 2026 Financial Results

RLX Technology Announces Unaudited Third Quarter 2026 Financial Results

PR Newswire

SHENZHEN, China, Nov. 20, 2026

SHENZHEN, China, Nov. 20, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- RLX Technology Inc. ("RLX Technology" or the "Company") (NYSE: RLX), a leading global branded e-vapor company, today announced its unaudited financial results for the third quarter ended September 30, 2026.

Third Quarter 2026 Financial Highlights

  • Net revenues were RMB1,916.6 million (US$285.9 million) in the third quarter of 2026, increasing by 69.7% from RMB1,129.3 million in the same period of 2025.
  • Gross profit increased by 26.7% to RMB446.6 million (US$66.6 million) in the third quarter of 2026.
  • Gross margin was 23.3% in the third quarter of 2026, compared with 31.2% in the same period of 2025, primarily due to a change in the revenue mix following the consolidation of the Company's newly acquired European entity.
  • Non-GAAP income from operations[1] was RMB143.8 million (US$21.4 million) in the third quarter of 2026, compared with RMB187.8 million in the same period of 2025.
  • U.S. GAAP net income was RMB147.1 million (US$21.9 million) in the third quarter of 2026, compared with RMB206.8 million in the same period of 2025.
  • Non-GAAP net income[1] was RMB235.6 million (US$35.1 million) in the third quarter of 2026, compared with RMB295.4 million in the same period of 2025.

"The third quarter marked a defining inflection point for RLX as we integrated our newly acquired European distribution platform with our existing retail footprint, evolving into a leading global smoke-free brand," said Ms. Ying (Kate) Wang, Co-founder, Chairperson, and Chief Executive Officer of RLX Technology. "We now possess end-to-end capabilities spanning global product innovation, supply chain execution, and direct route-to-market reach, while always placing our brands at the heart of adult consumers' choices worldwide. By pairing these strengths with dedicated local field teams and an open, multi-brand ecosystem philosophy, we are gaining sharper retail insights that will empower us to tailor products to local consumer preferences, scale our multi-category portfolio, and capture market share as shifting global regulations reshape the industry."

Mr. Chao Lu, Chief Financial Officer of RLX Technology, commented, "We delivered strong third quarter financial results, with the consolidation driving a surge in net revenues to RMB1.92 billion, up 69.7% year over year. International markets contributed 86.5% of our top line. While our blended gross margin now reflects the consolidation of the distribution business, we maintained solid non-GAAP profitability, improved working capital efficiency, and achieved a healthy sequential rebound in operating cash flow. Looking ahead, we are actively lifting our European platform's margins through supply chain optimization and capital deployment, while navigating transitional working capital needs related to the UK's October introduction of an excise duty. Supported by RMB13.48 billion in total financial assets, we have the financial flexibility to fund global brand expansion, deliver long-term sustainable growth, and maintain strong shareholder returns."

Third Quarter 2026 Financial Results

Net revenues were RMB1,916.6 million (US$285.9 million) in the third quarter of 2026, increasing by 69.7% from RMB1,129.3 million in the same period of 2025. The increase was primarily due to the consolidation of the Company's newly acquired European entity in July 2026. Net revenues from international business represented 86.5% of net revenues for the period.

Gross profit was RMB446.6 million (US$66.6 million) in the third quarter of 2026, increasing by 26.7% from RMB352.6 million in the same period of 2025.

Gross margin was 23.3% in the third quarter of 2026, compared with 31.2% in the same period of 2025, primarily due to a change in the revenue mix following the consolidation of the Company's newly acquired European entity.

Operating expenses were RMB407.1 million (US$60.7 million) in the third quarter of 2026, compared with RMB259.3 million in the same period of 2025. The increase was primarily due to higher salary and welfare expenses and increased shipping and logistics costs.

Selling expenses were RMB182.9 million (US$27.3 million) in the third quarter of 2026, compared with RMB132.3 million in the same period of 2025, primarily due to increases in salary and welfare expenses and shipping and logistics costs.

General and administrative expenses were RMB185.9 million (US$27.7 million) in the third quarter of 2026, compared with RMB85.7 million in the same period of 2025, primarily due to higher salary and welfare expenses and legal and other consulting fees.

Research and development expenses were RMB38.3 million (US$5.7 million) in the third quarter of 2026, compared with RMB41.3 million in the same period of 2025.

U.S. GAAP income from operations was RMB39.5 million (US$5.9 million) in the third quarter of 2026, compared with RMB93.3 million in the same period of 2025.

Non-GAAP income from operations was RMB143.8 million (US$21.4 million) in the third quarter of 2026, compared with RMB187.8 million in the same period of 2025.

Income tax expense was RMB43.6 million (US$6.5 million) in the third quarter of 2026, compared with RMB45.9 million in the same period of 2025.

U.S. GAAP net income was RMB147.1 million (US$21.9 million) in the third quarter of 2026, compared with RMB206.8 million in the same period of 2025.

Non-GAAP net income was RMB235.6 million (US$35.1 million) in the third quarter of 2026, compared with RMB295.4 million in the same period of 2025.

U.S. GAAP basic and diluted net income per American depositary share ("ADS") were RMB0.131 (US$0.020) and RMB0.123 (US$0.018), respectively, in the third quarter of 2026, compared with U.S. GAAP basic and diluted net income per ADS of RMB0.167 and RMB0.157, respectively, in the same period of 2025.

Non-GAAP basic and diluted net income per ADS[2] were RMB0.186 (US$0.028) and RMB0.175 (US$0.026), respectively, in the third quarter of 2026, compared with non-GAAP basic and diluted net income per ADS of RMB0.236 and RMB0.221, respectively, in the same period of 2025.

[1] Non-GAAP net income and non-GAAP income from operations are non-GAAP financial measures. For more information on the Company's non-GAAP financial measures, please see the section "Non-GAAP Financial Measures" and the table captioned "Unaudited Reconciliation of GAAP and Non-GAAP Results" set forth at the end of this press release.

[2] Non-GAAP basic and diluted net income per ADS is a non-GAAP financial measure. For more information on the Company's non-GAAP financial measures, please see the section "Non-GAAP Financial Measures" and the table captioned "Unaudited Reconciliation of GAAP and Non-GAAP Results" set forth at the end of this press release.

Balance Sheet and Cash Flow

As of September 30, 2026, the Company had cash and cash equivalents, restricted cash, short-term bank deposits, net, short-term investments, long-term bank deposits, net, and long-term investment securities, net, of RMB13,482.8 million (US$2,011.0 million), compared with RMB13,883.4 million as of June 30, 2026. In the third quarter of 2026, net cash generated from operating activities was RMB40.0 million (US$6.0 million).

Non-GAAP Financial Measures

The Company uses non-GAAP net income, non-GAAP income from operations and non-GAAP basic and diluted net income per ADS, each a non-GAAP financial measure, in evaluating its operating results and for financial and operational decision-making purposes. Non-GAAP net income represents net income excluding share-based compensation expenses, amortization and depreciation of assets arising from fair value step-up in business acquisitions, and tax effects on non-GAAP adjustments. Non-GAAP income from operations represents net income from operations excluding share-based compensation expenses and amortization and depreciation of assets arising from fair value step-up in business acquisitions. Non-GAAP basic and diluted net income per ADS is computed using non-GAAP net income attributable to RLX Technology Inc. and the same number of ADSs used in the U.S. GAAP basic and diluted net income per ADS calculation.

The Company presents these non-GAAP financial measures because they are used by the management to evaluate its operating performance and formulate business plans. The Company believes that they help identify underlying trends in its business that could otherwise be distorted by the effect of certain expenses that are included in net income. The Company also believes that the use of the non-GAAP measures facilitates investors' assessment of its operating performance, as they could provide useful information about its operating results, enhance the overall understanding of its past performance and future prospects, and allow for greater visibility with respect to key metrics used by the management in its financial and operational decision making.

The non-GAAP financial measures are not defined under U.S. GAAP and are not presented in accordance with U.S. GAAP. The non-GAAP financial measures have limitations as analytical tools. They should not be considered in isolation or construed as an alternative to net income, basic and diluted net income per ADS or any other measure of performance or as an indicator of its operating performance. Investors are encouraged to review its historical non-GAAP financial measures against the most directly comparable U.S. GAAP measures. The non-GAAP financial measures here may not be comparable to similarly titled measures presented by other companies. Other companies may calculate similarly titled measures differently, limiting their usefulness as comparative measures to our data. The Company encourages investors and others to review its financial information in its entirety and not rely on any single financial measure.

For more information on the non-GAAP financial measures, please see the table captioned "Unaudited Reconciliation of GAAP and non-GAAP Results" set forth at the end of this press release.

data.title: Global Bond Yields Fall as Investors Seek Safe-Haven Assets — Update
data.description:
By Miriam Mukuru

Yields on U.S., U.K., and eurozone government bonds dropped on Friday as risk-off sentiment continued to drive demand to safe-haven assets.

The 10-year Treasury yield fell 5.6 basis points to 4.996%, while the U.K. 10-year yield dropped 4.5 bps to 5.271%, according to Tradeweb. Ten-year German Bund yields declined 6.2 bps to 3.339%.

A record initial public offering by Anthropic, which raised $81 billion, failed to revive appetite for artificial-intelligence stocks. Investors continued to question whether the enormous investments in the AI industry would pay off given the rising public resistance toward the industry.

"The blockbuster debut [IPO] couldn't sweep those worries under the rug," Ipek Ozkardeskaya, senior analyst at Swissquote, said in a note.

Asian and European stocks sold off on Friday as sentiment continued to deteriorate even after some positive news in the tech industry this week.

"When neither a blockbuster Nvidia beat nor the largest IPO in history can lift the tape, market psychology has fundamentally flipped from dip-buying to structural de-risking," Patrick Munnelly, partner at Tickmill Group, said in a note.

High borrowing costs also raise concerns about AI companies' ability to continue raising funds to finance their massive expansion.

"The scale of the Democratic win in the midterm [elections] has deepened worry that policymakers could push for slower data-center spending," David Groman, global equity strategist at Citi, said in a note.

The concerns about the tech and AI sector are driving the flight to safety, causing government bond yields to drop, Groman said.

Write to Miriam Mukuru at miriam.mukuru@wsj.com

data.title: Al Shera’a, DEWA’s Headquarters, Wins First Place in the YeS Honor Awards at the COP31 International Sustainable Buildings Competition
data.description:
Al Shera’a, DEWA’s Headquarters, Wins First Place in the YeS Honor Awards at the COP31 International Sustainable Buildings Competition

In a new achievement that underscores Dubai’s pioneering position in smart and sustainable buildings, Al Shera’a, the headquarters of Dubai Electricity and Water Authority (DEWA), has won the first place in the YeS Honor Award–Sustainable Design category, in the COP31 International Sustainable Buildings Competition. The award was launched by the COP31 Presidency with the support of the Global Alliance for Buildings and Construction, hosted by the United Nations Environment Programme, during COP31 in Antalya, Türkiye.

This press release features multimedia. View the full release here: https://www.businesswire.com/news/home/20261118255551/en/

HE Saeed Mohammed Al Tayer, MD&CEO of DEWA, received the award in the presence of HE Amna bint Abdullah Al Dahak, UAE Minister of Climate Change and Environment, from HE Hasan Suver, Deputy Minister of Environment, Urbanisation and Climate Change of the Republic of Türkiye, representing the COP31 Presidency.

The competition attracted more than 1,000 buildings from 99 countries, evaluated by an international jury of experts appointed by UNEP. The award recognises excellence in sustainable design, indoor environmental quality, resource selection and energy performance. Al Shera’a was selected for its integration of smart building technologies, sustainable design principles and clean energy solutions, enhancing resource efficiency and environmental performance.

Al Shera’a features an integrated cognitive system that seamlessly connects and coordinates all operational systems. The system incorporates more than 110,000 smart sensors that monitor environmental and operational data in real time, alongside more than 1,500 wireless access points and over 3,200 network devices. It generates more than 1.9 million automated control commands daily, enhancing operational integration and efficiency.

Al Shera’a generates more than 7,500 megawatt-hours of renewable energy annually through photovoltaic (PV) solar panels covering more than 26,000 square metres across its roof and façades, enabling it to generate more clean energy than it consumes. Its solar PV systems have a combined installed capacity of approximately five megawatts (MW), distributed across two main systems. The first comprises 251 building-integrated photovoltaic panels covering approximately 9,000 square feet of façade area, with an installed capacity of 187 kilowatts (kW). The second comprises approximately 8,400 solar panels installed on the roof, façade fins, at ground level and on solar shading structures. The rooftop panels cover more than 200,000 square feet.

data.title: Equinor Fends Off Cyberattack Detected Earlier This Week
data.description:
By Dominic Chopping

Equinor said Friday that it had stopped a dayslong cyberattack that had targeted some of its systems.

The Norwegian energy company detected the attack on Tuesday but said it wasn't a virus attack, so there was no chance of it spreading, and that it also didn't appear to be specifically targeting Equinor.

Production has been running as normal throughout, and there are no signs that data has been stolen or altered, it said.

"There is also no indication that the attack has had any negative consequences for employees, partners or suppliers," the company said.

Equinor has been in talks with national security authorities, and the incident has been reported to police.

data.title: China's climate practices take center stage at COP31: cross-sector collaboration between meteorology and energy offers a Chinese approach to global climate adaptation
data.description:
China's climate practices take center stage at COP31: cross-sector collaboration between meteorology and energy offers a Chinese approach to global climate adaptation

China's climate practices take center stage at COP31: cross-sector collaboration between meteorology and energy offers a Chinese approach to global climate adaptation

PR Newswire

ANTALYA, Türkiye, Nov. 20, 2026

ANTALYA, Türkiye, Nov. 20, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- A thematic side event titled "From Early Warning to Energy Action: Pathways for Global Climate Diplomacy and Cooperation" was successfully held in the Blue Zone in Antalya, Türkiye, on November 13, during the 31st UN Climate Change Conference.

The event was jointly hosted by the United Nations Institute for Training and Research and the Public Meteorological Service Centre of the China Meteorological Administration (National Early Warning Information Release Center), with strategic support from China Energy News, the foreign affairs working committee of the China Energy Research Society, and the China Institute of Energy Economics Research.

Against the backdrop of increasingly severe global climate risks, the Climate Leadership Impact (CLI) initiative, jointly established by China Energy News, the China Energy Research Society and a number of other institutions and enterprises, was also officially launched. As a cross-sector collaboration platform, CLI aims to promote deeper integration between the meteorological and energy sectors across four key areas: risk governance and financial support, AI-powered forecasting and decision-making tools, coordinated clean energy dispatch, and interdisciplinary talent development.

During the event, CLI also presented the latest findings of its report, From Early Warning to Energy Action: 2026 Innovation Showcase on China's Corporate Actions and Collaborative Practices.

Amid intensifying global climate change and growing risks from extreme weather, coordinating the low-carbon transition with climate adaptation and ensuring the security of energy systems have become major challenges facing the international community. Guided by its goals of peaking carbon emissions and achieving carbon neutrality, China is advancing its new energy security strategy of "four revolutions and one cooperation" and accelerating the development of a new energy system. As climate risks increasingly affect energy infrastructure and the balance between supply and demand, integrating meteorological information throughout the entire energy industry chain has become a shared priority across the sector.

It was against this backdrop that the initiative to share the findings of "From Climate Early Warnings to Energy Action" was launched under the framework of the CLI.

The working team began soliciting case studies in mid-June 2026. Over approximately four and a half months, the report underwent multiple rounds of refinement, including outline development, case selection, initial drafting, expert reviews, verification by participating enterprises and simultaneous revisions in Chinese and English. During the process, experts from various fields, including the China Electricity Council, China Huaneng Group and meteorological authorities, provided rigorous reviews to ensure the report's scientific rigor, practical value for the industry and effectiveness in international communication.

China's Experience

Dr Wang Jingyu, assistant director of the national key laboratory of advanced electromagnetic technology at Huazhong University of Science and Technology and an associate research fellow, who led the main report-writing team, presented its findings at the event.

The report systematically reviews innovative practices by Chinese enterprises and research institutions and summarizes the technical pathways and supporting mechanisms for translating early warnings into concrete action. It highlights three key insights:

First, coordinated progress. The low-carbon transition in the energy sector and climate adaptation should advance in tandem, allowing emissions reduction achievements and energy system security to reinforce each other.

Second, targeted application. The key is to integrate meteorological and climate information with equipment conditions, network structures and energy consumption needs, so as to identify priority areas for protection and determine the appropriate timing for action.

Third, comprehensive support. Policy support and services, market-based financing, corporate governance and talent collaboration provide a strong foundation for the sustained implementation of technological advances.

In terms of practical applications, the report covers four major areas: energy transition and climate risks, the operational application of forecasting and early warning systems, policy and service support, and China's practical experience. It features 16 case studies across six categories, including renewable energy output forecasting, energy infrastructure protection, power grid risk assessment, and dispatch and maintenance, ensuring energy supplies for key users and power restoration, flexible adjustment of energy supply and demand, and emissions reduction and carbon sequestration.

These cases not only demonstrate measurable achievements in improving renewable energy integration, ensuring energy supply security, reducing disaster-related losses and enhancing operational efficiency, but also show how some of China's technologies and models have already been applied overseas. They offer valuable Chinese experience for the global energy sector in addressing climate change and advancing the development of new energy systems.
